# Source 119 — White House: EO 14365 "Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence"

- **URL:** https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/12/eliminating-state-law-obstruction-of-national-artificial-intelligence-policy/
- **Publisher:** The White House (Presidential Actions)
- **Published:** 2025-12-11
- **Type:** Executive Order (official text)
- **Status:** fetched 2026-09-14 (full text, http 200)

## Key claims (as stated in source)
- **EO 14365, signed December 11, 2025** (page URL slug references "eliminating state law obstruction"; title "Ensuring a National Policy Framework for Artificial Intelligence").
- Purpose: US AI leadership requires companies "free to innovate without cumbersome regulation"; **excessive State regulation** creates a "patchwork of 50 different regulatory regimes," increasingly forces "ideological bias" into models (cites a **Colorado law banning "algorithmic discrimination"** that "may even force AI models to produce false results"), and sometimes impermissibly regulates beyond State borders.
- Policy: sustain/enhance US global AI dominance **through a minimally burdensome national policy framework for AI**.
- **Sec. 3 — AI Litigation Task Force:** Within **30 days**, the Attorney General shall establish a Task Force whose sole responsibility is to **challenge State AI laws inconsistent with the order**, on grounds including unconstitutional regulation of interstate commerce, preemption by existing Federal regulations, or other unlawfulness.
- **Sec. 4 — Evaluation of State AI Laws:** Within **90 days**, the Secretary of Commerce shall publish an evaluation identifying onerous State AI laws that conflict with the order (e.g., laws requiring models to alter truthful outputs, or compelling disclosure/reporting that may violate the First Amendment).
- **Sec. 5 — Restrictions on State Funding:** Within 90 days, the Secretary of Commerce (via the Assistant Secretary for Communications and Information) shall issue a Policy Notice making **States with onerous AI laws ineligible for non-deployment BEAD funds** (Broadband Equity, Access, and Deployment) to the maximum extent allowed; agencies to assess conditioning discretionary grants on States not enacting/challenging conflicting AI laws.
- **Sec. 6 — Federal Reporting/Disclosure Standard:** Within 90 days of the Sec. 4 identification, the FCC Chairman shall initiate a proceeding on whether to adopt a Federal reporting/disclosure standard for AI models that preempts conflicting State laws.
- **Sec. 7 — FTC preemption:** Within 90 days, the FTC Chairman shall issue a policy statement on applying the FTC Act's prohibition on unfair/deceptive acts (15 U.S.C. 45) to AI models, explaining when State laws requiring alterations to truthful outputs are preempted.
- **Sec. 8 — Legislation:** Special Advisor for AI and Crypto + APST to jointly prepare a legislative recommendation for a uniform Federal AI framework preempting conflicting State laws; **shall not propose preempting** State laws on (i) child safety protections, (ii) AI compute/data center infrastructure (other than generally applicable permitting reforms), (iii) State government procurement/use of AI, (iv) other topics.
